description: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, as measured by the performance of various multilingual BERT models. The horizontal axis displays different language families—IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic—while the vertical axis quantifies the effect on a scale from 0 to 30. Each language family has a cluster of bars representing different models: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). Error bars, indicating standard deviation, are shown above each bar. For instance, in the IE-Indic family, mBERT-L₂ shows a low effect (~2), whereas XLM-B₂ shows a high effect (~22). In the Semitic family, XLM-L₂ has the highest effect (~16), while mBERT-L₂ has a negative effect (~-4). The chart reveals that the effect varies significantly across models and language families, with some models showing strong positive effects (e.g., XLM-B₂ in IE-Indic) and others showing negative or minimal effects (e.g., mBERT-L₂ in Semitic). The overall pattern suggests that the impact of context masking on case tasks is highly dependent on both the model architecture and the linguistic characteristics of the language family.
